location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots (label stamping via `_compose_labels_yaml`)
issue: The contract says the version process stamps 'its PS container' with `psm.slots=<cost>` 'next to the ownership labels (`_compose_labels_yaml` in ps-flashlight-run.py)'. That helper (and `_label_flags` on the manual path) is the single source of labels for the DB service, the PS service and the network, and it is shared with Layer 2 (flashlight) and Layer 5 (scenario) containers. Following the pointer literally puts `psm.slots` on the DB container too (each boot counted twice) and on Layer 2/5 containers (which the decided policy says are not E2E and must not count).
implementation_impact: An implementer extending `owner_labels()`/`_compose_labels_yaml` doubles every E2E boot's cost in `docker ps --filter label=psm.slots` and makes flashlight/scenario boots consume E2E slots, so the default cap of 6 admits about half the intended work and tier 1 falls into `--sequential-browsers` or `no-slots` -> `blocked-infra`.
suggestion: State that `psm.slots` is a separate label added only to the PS service of an E2E boot (compose `ps:` block and the manual `docker run` of `ps_container`), never through `owner_labels()`, and add a test that a booted E2E version shows exactly one container with `psm.slots` and that a Layer 2 boot shows none.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots ('Every running labelled container counts, including an orphan whose owner died, until --cleanup-orphans removes it')
issue: The count is daemon-wide (other WSL distros, other temp dirs), but `cleanup_decision` refuses to delete containers whose labels show `foreign-host` or `foreign-pid-ns`. An orphan left by a dead run in another WSL distro therefore counts against the cap for good: this distro's `--cleanup-orphans` will never remove it, and name/prune removal is forbidden. The contract offers no way out. Separately, psm containers started by pre-upgrade scripts carry no `psm.slots` label, so they load the daemon without being counted.
implementation_impact: After one crashed run in a sibling distro, every session runs with a permanently lower cap. Two such orphans at cost 2 plus a warm keeper can push every cell into `no-slots` and then `blocked-infra`. The only remedy the operator has is a forbidden command.
suggestion: Define how foreign-namespace orphans are handled: either the count excludes containers whose owner is provably dead or unverifiable for longer than N hours (logged as `slot-ignored`), or `--list-jobs` reports them with the exact cleanup command to run from the owning distro. Also say that unlabelled `psm.run` containers from older scripts count as 1 slot, or document that they are ignored.

location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade > Fresh (`source_fingerprint` over every file under the module directory except `.git/`)
issue: The PSM workflow writes its own artifacts into the module directory: psm-develop writes `<module-path>/.psm-develop-plan.md` and `.psm-develop-plan.json` and updates their status after verification, psm-module-context writes `<module-path>/.memlog.md`, and psm-ideate writes `.psm-ideas.md`. Editor swap files and `node_modules/` from front-end builds also sit there. All of them are in the fingerprint, so any bookkeeping write stales every E2E cell, even though none of it ships or affects runtime. The claim that 'this is the set the install copies' also fails for `.git/`, which `cp -r /ps-module-src` does copy.
implementation_impact: psm-develop's normal sequence (validate headless, then mark the item 'diterapkan' in the plan files) immediately makes the evidence it just produced stale. The next validation re-proves all 6 cells for a markdown edit, which defeats the speed goal. A fingerprint walk over `node_modules` on WSL also slows every plan call.
suggestion: Define an explicit exclusion list shared by the fingerprint and the install copy (at least `.git/`, `.psm-*`, `.memlog.md`, `node_modules/`, editor temp files), or fingerprint exactly what `INSTALL_SH` copies after applying the same exclusions. Add a test that editing `.psm-develop-plan.json` leaves every cell fresh.

issue: The field list has no module identity (module name or resolved module path). Today `ps-aggregate.py` rejects layer files whose `module` differs from the static scan's ('bukti module lain tak boleh masuk vonis ini'). The history files are keyed only by the module basename, so two modules with the same folder name (a fork, a copy under another path) share one history, and nothing in a record can reject the other module's lines.
implementation_impact: The aggregate and the plan silently mix records from another module with the same basename. Freshness usually turns them stale, but `blocked-infra`, focus-cell selection ('newest run holds the failing record') and `corrupt-history` all read those records. An existing safety check is lost without anyone deciding to drop it.
suggestion: Add `module` (name) and `module_path` (resolved) to the required record fields. Plan and aggregate skip records whose `module_path` differs from the current one, with a note, and the aggregate keeps its exit-2 identity check for histories.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures and Identical findings
issue: Confirmation keeps 'parallel findings whose (scenario, action) also fails in the rerun', and the CAP-7 test compares (version, browser, scenario, action, ok, conclusive) tuples. But `assemble_findings` in ps-e2e-run.py emits findings with `id`, `message`, `browser`, `scenario` and `source`, and no `action`, `ok`, `conclusive` or step index. The action appears only inside `id`, and a scenario often repeats the same action (several `expect_text` or `goto` steps), so (scenario, action) cannot tell which step failed.
implementation_impact: An implementer either parses `id` strings or invents fields. A parallel failure at step 3 is 'confirmed' by an unrelated sequential failure at step 7 with the same action name, and the identical-findings test cannot be written against the current finding shape.
suggestion: Extend the finding schema with `action`, `step` (index within the scenario), `ok` and `conclusive`, and define the confirmation and comparison key as (scenario, step, action). List the schema change under Runner.

location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures (rerun-seq against 'the same container')
issue: The sequential confirmation runs after both parallel passes, against a DB that both engines have already mutated (orders placed, stock decremented, vouchers consumed, configuration toggled by BO setup scenarios). Nothing resets the DB first. A failure caused by parallel interference (for example a shared product's stock exhausted by two concurrent checkouts) leaves state behind that makes the sequential rerun fail too, so a parallel-induced failure gets 'confirmed'. The reference sequential run in the identical-findings test sees one prior pass, not two, so the two runs do not start from comparable states.
implementation_impact: Parallel-mode artefacts can still block `ready` while posing as reproduced findings, which is exactly what r3-q1 meant to prevent, and the CAP-7 identical-findings test will be flaky on modules with stateful scenarios.
suggestion: Before `rerun-seq`, restore the DB to a baseline captured after `install`/`warmup-bo` (reuse the warm `reset-db` mechanism, or `snapshot_db`/`restore_db` from ps-scenario-run.py), and state that the identical-findings reference run uses the same baseline before each engine. Otherwise, document that confirmation is best-effort for stateful scenarios.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > step 2 `blocked-not-gradeable` vs Evidence record ('A record with a missing field is never gate-grade')
issue: Step 2 fires when 'some configured cell's newest gate-grade record is a pass that a rerun ... cannot make passing gate-grade (... or a missing field)'. A record with a missing field is never gate-grade by definition, so that branch can never match. The result is that a fresh, cold, full, conclusive `pass` with a missing field (runner bug, partially upgraded runner) is neither gate-grade, nor `blocked-not-gradeable`, nor a `blocked-infra` cause (which covers only inconclusive reasons, `inconclusive-steps` and `browser-notes`).
implementation_impact: The plan emits the same step for that cell forever. The interactive orchestrator, which 'runs exactly e2e_next_cells', reboots the cell on every iteration and gets the same missing-field record each time, an unbounded loop of cold boots.
suggestion: Either classify 'cold, full, conclusive record with a missing required field' as its own reason (`incomplete-record`) that counts as an infra cause for `blocked-infra`, or move the missing-field case out of step 2 and say that such a record is treated as `inconclusive` with reason `incomplete-record`. Add a test that two such records in one session end the loop.

issue: The two steps test freshness in opposite ways. Step 5 promotes when the focus cell 'has a fresh pass record of any grade', even if a newer fresh fail exists. Step 6 refuses when the canary 'has no fresh fail record' is false, even if a newer fresh pass exists. On the same fingerprint (the operator reruns to check flakiness without patching, or a warm failed-only pass follows a warm fail before any patch), step 6 can never match again: every derivation falls to step 7 `focus`, which repeats while the old fresh fail remains, until an unrelated patch changes the fingerprint.
implementation_impact: A flaky canary scenario traps the loop in tier 0 with green warm runs and no promotion, and the opposite asymmetry in step 5 lets a non-canary focus cell promote to `cold-version` while its newest fresh record is a fail.
suggestion: Make both conditions use the same newest-record rule, for example 'the newest fresh record of the cell (any boot, any scenario set) is `pass`', and add plan tests for fail-then-pass and pass-then-fail on one fingerprint for both the canary and a non-canary focus cell.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > step 2 `blocked-not-gradeable` (authored_assertions 0 / scenario_notes non-empty) and its ordering before `gate`
issue: For a module that ships no authored E2E scenarios (smoke-only), or one with a single spec that triggers a note (no `expect_*` action, or a spec deleted but still tracked by git), the canary's first cold run produces a pass that is not gate-grade-passing, and step 2 ends the E2E loop before tier 1. Today such a module still gets the universal smoke (a fatal error, an HTTP 500 on the module page) on every version and both browsers. Under the new plan, 1.7.8 and 8.1 are never booted for E2E at all.
implementation_impact: This regresses coverage: a module that fatals only on 1.7.8 under the smoke test is no longer detected by Layer 4. The report shows only `blocked-not-gradeable`, with no per-version smoke signal, although `ready` is false for an unrelated reason.
suggestion: Let `blocked-not-gradeable` stop gate-grade promotion but still run tier 1 once for smoke evidence (recorded and reported, never counted toward `ready`), or state explicitly in Non-goals that smoke-only modules lose cross-version smoke coverage and get it only through `--require` without `e2e`.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container (CAP-5) > Owner / 'A keeper with another owner is never attached, reset, reused or stopped' + Evidence record > `session`
issue: The keeper belongs to the validation session token, and a keeper with a different owner token can be neither reused nor stopped. The contract never defines when an interactive validation session starts or ends (each psm-validate invocation? each conversation?). If Budi re-invokes psm-validate on the same module after the orchestrator lost context or crashed, the new session cold-boots ('foreign-keeper') while the old keeper keeps its slot, its RAM and its container for up to 60 idle minutes, and the new session is not allowed to stop it.
implementation_impact: Each restart of the interactive flow leaks a warm container for an hour on a shared WSL daemon, which is the saturation the slot cap exists to prevent. The same undefined lifecycle decides when `blocked-infra` resets, so its behaviour also varies with how the orchestrator invents tokens.
suggestion: Define the session token's lifecycle (created at On Activation, persisted in `<psm_reports_dir>/<module>-session.json`, reused until Phase 2 ends or the operator starts a fresh validation). Let the same operator's new session stop a previous session's keeper for the same module when that session's orchestrator is no longer active, logging it, or list stale keepers with the `--stop-job` command in the activation report.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields (`session`) and 'null for fields no engine produced' vs 'A record with a missing field is never gate-grade'
issue: The contract does not say whether `--session` is mandatory on `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` and `ps-plan-layers.py`, or what a record looks like when it is absent. It also does not say whether a key present with value `null` counts as a 'missing field'. Engine-produced fields are explicitly `null` for not-run cells, and `session` would be `null` for any caller that omits the flag (the current run-phases commands, ad-hoc runs).
implementation_impact: Implementers will disagree on whether `session: null` records are gate-grade. If they are not, every gate run by an un-updated caller silently fails to count. If they are, `blocked-infra` can never trigger for those runs because 'both carry the current --session' never matches.
suggestion: Make `--session` required for `--layer e2e` and for the plan (exit 2 when absent). List the fields that must be present and non-null for gate-grade (for example `session`, `source_fingerprint`, `image_tag`, `boot`, `scenario_set`, `authored_assertions`), and say that `null` counts as missing only for those.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage ('the cell gets reason corrupt-history ... until a newer valid record exists')
issue: 'Newer' is defined everywhere else as a higher `started_at`, but an unparseable line has no readable `started_at`, so nothing is newer or older than it. Records are also not appended in `started_at` order: `not-run` and `no-slots` records carry the admission time, and records are appended after the child exits.
implementation_impact: One implementation keeps the cell in `corrupt-history` forever, because no record can be proven newer than the garbage line. Another clears it as soon as any valid line exists anywhere in the file, including lines before the corruption. The plan's first-priority reason is therefore unstable.
suggestion: Define it by file position: a corrupt line poisons the cell until a valid record appears after it in the file. Say whether the corrupt line also hides valid records before it (recommended: no), and add a test with a valid record before and after the corrupt line.

location: SPEC.md > CAP-3 success ('a cap of one cell at a time, three queued cells ... no bring-up for them') vs cell-contract.md > Runner / Slots
issue: Admission is per version child, not per cell: one `--cells V:chromium+firefox` child is one boot, and with a 1-slot cap it runs in `--sequential-browsers` mode. If two of the 'three queued cells' share a version, that version's bring-up has already happened, and the second engine is stopped by the in-process fail-fast rule, not by ps-run-layer. The test fixture does not say which case it covers, and 'a cap of one cell' is not a configurable unit: the cap is `psm_e2e_slots`, counted daemon-wide.
implementation_impact: The acceptance test is ambiguous and environment-dependent. On a shared daemon where other sessions hold slots, `--slots 1` can mean no cell is admitted at all, so the test hits `no-slots` instead of fail-fast.
suggestion: Rewrite the CAP-3 success to use three cells on three distinct versions with `--slots 1`, plus a second case for two engines of one version in sequential fallback. Require the test to stub the daemon-wide slot count so that other sessions' containers do not affect it.

location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 / tier-matrix.md vs SKILL.md Lapis 4 visual verification (model-judged blocking findings written to `<module>-adversarial.json`)
issue: Today the interactive orchestrator reviews E2E screenshots and writes visual defects it judges blocking into the adversarial layer file. The tiered contract never says which tier's screenshots are reviewed (warm iterations, the cold canary, tier 1), and a visual finding has no (version, browser) cell, so it cannot become a focus cell or trigger a loop-back. Layer 3 output from before a patch is declared stale and regenerated, which would also discard visual findings made in tier 0.
implementation_impact: A visual defect seen on 1.7.8 × Firefox in tier 1 blocks `ready` through the adversarial file but drives no `e2e_step`. The operator patches with no defined re-proof path, and the regenerated Layer 3 file may drop the finding, so it can disappear without being fixed.
suggestion: State where visual review happens (recommended: on tier 1 and cold-canary screenshots only). Record visual blocking findings per cell, for example as a `visual_findings` field appended to that cell's history or a separate per-cell file, so a cell with a visual blocker is 'failing' for focus derivation. Also state that the Layer 3 regeneration rule does not discard them.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > step 3 `blocked-infra` (same infra cause = `reason` of an inconclusive record)
issue: Every `inconclusive` reason counts as an infra cause, including `stopped`, which ps-run-layer writes when the operator uses `--stop-job`. Two operator stops of the same cell in one session (for example stopping a slow run to patch a typo, before the patch lands) end the E2E loop as `blocked-infra`, even though nothing is wrong with the infrastructure.
implementation_impact: An operator who stops runs deliberately gets an unexpected loop termination and has to start a new validation session to continue, losing the session's warm keeper (see the owner-token rule).
suggestion: Exclude `stopped` (and `not-run`) from the infra causes counted by `blocked-infra`, and list the qualifying reasons explicitly (`crash`, `browser-unavailable`, `no-slots`, `parallel-unconfirmed`, `errors`, `install`, `launch-error`, `not-driven`, `inconclusive-steps`, `browser-notes`).

issue: The lock file lives inside the job registry directory. `_job_unregister` removes that directory only when it is empty (`path.parent.rmdir()`), so the leftover `.bo.lock` keeps every E2E job directory under `<tmp>/psm-jobs/` forever. Those directories are then iterated by `_registry_entries` / `--list-jobs` on every call. The contract also does not say who deletes the lock file.
implementation_impact: Registry directories accumulate without bound across runs. It is a small leak, but in exactly the registry that `--stop-job` and slot admission scan.
suggestion: Put the lock outside the registry (for example `<tmp>/psm-locks/<job>-<ver>.bo.lock`), or have the version process unlink it after both workers exit and before its own unregister, and add that to the teardown description.
